extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying to MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships (and their supervisors / institutional EU advisors), specifically NTNU applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and annotated template for preparing Part B (technical description) of MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship proposals (MSCA-PF-2024), covering how to address evaluation criteria (Excellence, Impact, Implementation), formatting/submission rules, and supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1.1 Quality and pertinence of the project's research and innovation objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and pertinence of the project’s research and innovation objectives (and the extent to which they are ambitious, and go beyond the state of the art). At a minimum: describe the quality and pertinence of the R&I objectives; are the objectives measurable and verifiable? Are they realistically achievable? Describe how your project goes beyond the state-of-the-art, and the extent to which the proposed work is ambitious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a concise 'sales pitch' (mini-abstract). Set the stage (problem + why care), present your solution (research questions/hypotheses, basis, preliminary results), and create a vision (expected results, beneficiaries, impacts). Include a short paragraph on training and career impact. Prefer placing state-of-the-art before objectives. Objectives must be specific, measurable, verifiable, realistically achievable (2-year European Fellowship usually: 2–3 research objectives recommended). Avoid weak verbs (investigate, study); prefer identify/develop/measure. Highlight objectives (bold/box). Ensure objectives map to work packages (recommended 1:1 ratio). Use explicit variables/hypotheses where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-of-the-art / Beyond state-of-the-art
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the relevant state-of-the-art and its limitations. Explain, in concrete terms, how the proposed research will overcome these limitations and go beyond the state-of-the-art (i.e. how is it conceptually novel?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give specific, up-to-date references; avoid overly general summaries. Provide enough context for evaluators to judge novelty without textbook-level detail. Consider a concise table (State-of-the-art / Planned research / Beyond state-of-the-art). Include your and your supervisor's prior contributions (published or promising unpublished findings) to build credibility and reduce perceived risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1.2 Soundness of the proposed methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe and explain the overall methodology, including the concepts, models and assumptions that underpin your work. Explain how this will enable delivery of the project's objectives, and refer to major challenges and how they will be overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present an overview of the workplan (visual PERT/Gantt) showing interplay between WPs and identifiable flows of results/data. Explain methods, data to be collected (how much, who/what), and analysis approaches. Justify choice of methods and demonstrate feasibility and relevant expertise. Ensure coherence between objectives and WPs; avoid introducing objective-defining information in WP descriptions. For secondments/non-academic placements describe precisely what will be done there and expected expertise gained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of methods and interdisciplinarity (sub-criterion of 1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how expertise and methods from different disciplines will be brought together and integrated in pursuit of objectives. If an interdisciplinary approach is unnecessary, provide a justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what knowledge, tools or methods are combined from different disciplines and why this integration is necessary to address the research questions. Highlight two-way knowledge transfer (e.g., your perspective vs supervisor's). If cross-sector (non-academic placement), emphasise how sector knowledge is integrated. Note: Horizon Europe requires justification if interdisciplinarity is not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender dimension and other diversity aspects (sub-criterion of 1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the gender dimension and other diversity aspects are taken into account in the project’s research and innovation content. If not relevant, provide justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This refers to content-level sex/gender and diversity analysis (biological and social/cultural factors), not team gender balance. Provide methods/approach for sex/gender/diversity analysis where relevant and refer to guidance links if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science practices (sub-criterion of 1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how appropriate open science practices are implemented as an integral part of the proposed methodology, adapted to the nature of your work, to increase the chances of delivering objectives (e.g. up to 1/2 page including research data management). If none are appropriate, justify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open science includes early/open sharing (pre-prints, preregistration), research output management, reproducibility measures, open access to outputs (publications, data, code), open peer review participation, and stakeholder/citizen involvement. Explain chosen practices and how they fit the project. Distinguish from outreach/communication, which should be in Impact section. See HE Programme Guide and video resources for evaluating open science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data management and FAIR principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants generating/collecting data and/or other research outputs must explain how data will be managed in line with the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise plan for data and other outputs: storage, metadata, sharing, preservation, and access levels. Refer to guidance in the HE Programme Guide. If open sharing is not appropriate, justify. Include research data management practices within the Open Science subsection (approx. 1/2 page recommended).

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-based systems: technical and social robustness (if AI used)
rubrics_metrics.description: If using, developing or deploying AI-based systems, demonstrate their technical robustness and suitability under the appropriate criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI systems should be technically robust, accurate, reproducible, and able to inform about possible failures/inaccuracies/errors proportionate to assessed risk. They should be socially robust (considering context), reliable (minimise unintentional/unexpected harm and safeguard physical/mental integrity), and able to provide suitable explanations of decision-making when significant impacts on people’s lives are possible. Be very descriptive about techniques and robustness when including AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work packages (WPs), tasks and coherence with objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe work packages and tasks: each WP should link to a corresponding objective; workflow should be organised as tasks (T1.1, T1.2...). Make clear expected results per WP and how they relate to other WPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend ~1:1 ratio between research objectives and research WPs. Use manageable number of tasks (~2–3 per WP). Include WP headings linking to objectives. Provide a visual overview (PERT/Gantt) showing flows of data/results. Avoid fragmentation: WPs should be integrated and coherent. Indicate methods, data collection amount, analysis, and justify feasibility and expertise. Use WP/task nomenclature across documents (Gantt, Section 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks and mitigation / risk assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify risks/challenges (conceptual or operational) that could prevent achieving objectives and indicate mitigation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess level of likelihood (Low/medium/high) and severity (Low/medium/high) taking account of mitigating measures. Focus on conceptual (e.g., falsified hypothesis) and operational risks (data sampling, analysis, instruments); avoid trivial risks. Use milestones to correspond to overcoming key risks. Locate riskier parts towards end of workplan to avoid project collapse early. Use preliminary data to reduce perceived risk. Consider indicating risk and probability in WP headings where useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1.3 Quality of supervision, training and two-way transfer of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality, appropriateness and feasibility of the supervision and training arrangements, and the two-way transfer of knowledge between the researcher and the host(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe supervision (role/profile of supervisor), training objectives (2–3 training objectives common: professional/technical skills, transferable/soft skills, communication/outreach), and plan them as a training WP if appropriate. Explain two-way knowledge transfer: what the researcher brings and what they will gain. For secondments/non-academic placements make clear what will be done and expertise gained. Provide evidence of supervisor and host expertise and track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.1 Enhancing the researcher's career prospects and skills (Impact — researcher development)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which the fellowship will enhance the researcher's career prospects and employability within and beyond academia, and the quality of the proposed measures for training and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain future career aspirations and how skills learned during the Fellowship will enable achieving career objectives. Link training objectives and planned activities to measurable career outcomes and employability. Include planned networking, secondments, placements, and professional training activities that demonstrate interdisciplinarity and intersectoral experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.2 Communication, dissemination and exploitation measures (Impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and effectiveness of the proposed measures to communicate, disseminate and exploit the project results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe target groups, channels, timing, expected uptake/impact, and how measures will lead to outcomes/use. Distinguish communication/dissemination/exploitation from open science practices (described under Excellence). Provide concrete plans and indicators for uptake, exploitation and dissemination; address how results will be made accessible to intended users/stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.3 Expected outcomes and longer-term impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The expected effects (outcomes) of the project over the medium term and the wider long-term impacts on society, economy and science enabled by the outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe outcomes (e.g., uptake by target groups) and long-term impacts (societal, environmental, economic, scientific). Provide concrete examples/metrics (e.g., number of adopters, capacity increases) and explain how dissemination/exploitation measures will foster uptake. Link results to intended outcomes and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.1 Quality and effectiveness of the work plan, management and resource allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Coherence, effectiveness and realistic-ness of the work plan (including tasks, deliverables, milestones, Gantt chart), appropriateness of the management structures and procedures, and justification of the resources (including access to facilities, equipment and infrastructure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear Gantt chart, specify deliverables and milestones (verifiable control points), show resource allocation and justification. Demonstrate that requested resources are appropriate and sufficient for WPs. Show management arrangements and how progress will be monitored and corrective actions taken. Use milestones to mark key decision/verification points.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3.2 Host organisation capacity, facilities and previous involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that the beneficiary has sufficient facilities and infrastructure to host and/or offer a suitable environment for training and transfer of knowledge to the recruited experienced researcher. Indicate previous and current involvement in up to 5 relevant EU, national or international research and training actions/projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List key research facilities, equipment, and infrastructure and explain their accessibility to the researcher. Provide evidence of host/department experience in relevant projects, and any links to associated partners. Show track record to host and support the fellow's development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and submission requirements (page limits, fonts, tagging, PDF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strict formatting and submission rules: Part B-1 (Sections 1–3) must not exceed 10 pages (all tables, figures, references included). Minimum font size 11 pt for body text; acceptable fonts specified. Document must be A4 with margins ≥15 mm. The document is tagged—do not delete tags. Part B must be submitted as two separate PDF files (B1 with page limit, B2 without).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excess pages will be made invisible after deadline; hyperlinks intended to circumvent page limits will be ignored. Upload final proposal at least 24 hours before deadline to avoid portal slowdowns. Use reference fonts unless legibility and page-count equivalence maintained. Ensure PDFs have embedded fonts (Adobe v3+).

rubrics_metrics.name: Part B-2 required content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Part B-2 (no page limit) must include the CV of the researcher, the capacity of participating organisation(s), and letters of commitment of associated partner(s) if applicable (only for Global Fellowships outgoing hosts and proposals with non-academic placement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B-2 must be a separate PDF. Ensure CVs and institutional capacity statements are clear and provide evidence of ability to host and supervise. Letters of commitment must meet minimum requirements (see Letters of commitment rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of commitment for associated partners (requirements and consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of commitment (for associated partners hosting outgoing phase or non-academic placements) must have heading or stamp from the institution, be up to date (not dated prior to call publication), demonstrate will to participate, and explain precise role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If letter fails to provide enough information (no signature, wrong references, outdated), experts may penalise proposal under Implementation. For Global Fellowship (GF) proposals, absence of a letter of commitment for the outgoing phase renders the proposal inadmissible (will not be evaluated). Experts will disregard contributions from associated partners without evidence of commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and use of deliverables and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliverables: reports sent to Commission/Agency to ensure effective monitoring (different types). Milestones: control points to chart progress, verifiable achievements enabling next project phases or decision points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use deliverables and milestones to show verifiable progress. Milestones can correspond to overcoming key risks or decisions (e.g., technology selection). Ensure deliverables and milestones are specific, time-bound and linked to WPs and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and security additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any additional ethics information that could not be included in Part A. Include any additional security screening information that was not in Part A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide thorough, accurate ethics and security details when needed; missing or incomplete information may affect admissibility or scoring. Use the additional sections only for items not possible to include elsewhere in the submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental considerations (MSCA Green Charter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the proposed project would strive to adhere to the MSCA Green Charter during its implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the MSCA Green Charter is non-binding and adherence will not be subject to evaluation, funded projects are strongly encouraged to take its principles into account. Describe measures to reduce environmental footprint where relevant.
